title: Psalm 46: God Is Our Refuge and Strength
summary: The psalm declares that God is his people's refuge and strength, so they will not fear even if the earth gives way and the mountains fall into the sea. A river gladdens the city of God, and God is within her, so she will not be moved while nations rage. The psalm ends with God's own voice: “Be still and know that I am God”, and a refrain that the LORD of Hosts is with us.
line: God is his people's refuge and strength, so they will not fear though the earth give way; he is within his city, and he calls them to be still and know that he is God.
guide: The psalm does not promise that nothing bad will happen; it says who is with you when it does. Say verse 1 into whatever your falling mountain is. Being still means letting go of control, so ask what you are gripping that God is asking you to drop.

stanzas.title: No fear, though the earth gives way
The river and the city of God
Come and see: God ends war, be still

verses.t: For the choirmaster. Of the sons of Korah. According to Alamoth. A song. God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in times of trouble.
Therefore we will not fear, though the earth is transformed and the mountains are toppled into the depths of the seas,
though their waters roar and foam and the mountains quake in the surge. Selah
There is a river whose streams delight the city of God, the holy place where the Most High dwells.
God is within her; she will not be moved. God will help her when morning dawns.
Nations rage, kingdoms crumble; the earth melts when He lifts His voice.
The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah
Come, see the works of the LORD, who brings devastation upon the earth.
He makes wars to cease throughout the earth; He breaks the bow and shatters the spear; He burns the shields in the fire.
“Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted over the earth.”
The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah
